title: Key terms (31) and which works they apply to

cards.back:
Definition: The ~1,000 years between the fall of Rome (ca. 400s CE) and the Renaissance (ca. 1400).
Applies to: Every Early Medieval, Romanesque, and Gothic work

Definition: Old English epic poem about a hero who kills monsters.
Applies to: Sutton Hoo purse (its treasure burials parallel Sutton Hoo)

Definition: Thin metal strips (cloisons) soldered to a surface form cells, filled with enamel, glass, or gems like garnet.
Applies to: Sutton Hoo purse

Definition: Using animal forms in decoration or design.
Applies to: Sutton Hoo purse, Book of Kells

Definition: European style ca. 1000-1200, "Roman-like": thick walls, rounded arches, barrel vaults, heavy massing.
Applies to: Morgan Madonna, Bayeux Tapestry

Definition: Container, often precious and ornate, that holds a saint's relics (body parts or belongings).
Applies to: Virgin of Jeanne d'Évreux (the fleur-de-lis held relics of Mary)

Definition: Sedes Sapientiae: Mary seated frontally with Christ on her lap; Mary is the throne, Christ is divine wisdom.
Applies to: Morgan Madonna

Definition: Decorating fabric by stitching colored thread onto it.
Applies to: Bayeux Tapestry (wool on linen)

Definition: Semicircular arch inherited from Rome; hallmark of Romanesque building.
Applies to: No focus work; Romanesque churches generally

Definition: Monastery room where monks copied and illuminated manuscripts by hand.
Applies to: Book of Kells

Definition: Continuous rounded-arch ceiling like a tunnel; heavy, needs thick walls, so few windows.
Applies to: No focus work; Romanesque churches generally

Definition: A pilgrim travels to a holy site to see relics; pilgrimage drove construction of big churches along the routes.
Applies to: Saint-Denis (Suger rebuilt partly for pilgrim crowds); Romanesque pilgrimage churches

Definition: Abbot of Saint-Denis who rebuilt its choir ca. 1140-44, creating the first Gothic architecture.
Applies to: Saint-Denis

Definition: Arch that peaks at the top; pushes weight more downward, allowing taller, thinner walls. Gothic hallmark.
Applies to: Saint-Denis

Definition: Vault framed by crossing stone ribs that carry the load, so the panels between can be thin and light.
Applies to: Saint-Denis

Definition: Stylized lily; symbol of the French monarchy and of the Virgin Mary.
Applies to: Virgin of Jeanne d'Évreux (she holds a fleur-de-lis scepter)

Definition: Exterior arch that braces upper walls from outside, so walls can be thin and full of windows.
Applies to: No focus work; Gothic cathedrals generally

Definition: Colored glass pieces held by lead strips forming images; a rose window is a large circular one with radiating tracery.
Applies to: Saint-Denis

Definition: Ornamental stonework holding the glass in a window, forming intricate patterns.
Applies to: Saint-Denis windows; Gothic windows generally

Definition: "New light": Suger's term for colored divine light through stained glass, meant to lift the soul to God.
Applies to: Saint-Denis
• Not one of the 5 Gothic design elements. Lux nova is how the stained-glass light was described

Definition: Small, precious objects in costly materials (gold, silver, enamel, gems) for royal or elite patrons.
Applies to: Virgin of Jeanne d'Évreux

Definition: Image of Mary mourning the dead Christ across her lap (Italian for "pity").
Applies to: Röttgen Pietà

Definition: Painting on wet plaster (buon fresco) so the pigment bonds into the wall as it dries; permanent.
Applies to: No current focus work. Contrast: the Last Supper is NOT fresco, it's a secco

Definition: Mathematical system where parallel lines (orthogonals) converge at a vanishing point to create depth on a flat surface.
Applies to: Gates of Paradise, Last Supper

Definition: Depth shown by making distant objects lighter, bluer, hazier, and less detailed.
Applies to: Gates of Paradise (shallower, softer relief in the distance)

Definition: Renaissance movement reviving classical Greek/Roman learning and celebrating human potential and the individual.
Applies to: Donatello's David, Primavera, Michelangelo's David, Gates of Paradise

Definition: Wealthy Florentine banking family who ruled Florence and funded artists.
Applies to: Donatello's David, Primavera

Definition: Paint of pigment mixed with egg yolk; dries fast with crisp, matte color.
Applies to: Primavera; also the Book of Kells pigments

Definition: "Light-dark": strong contrast of light and shadow to model forms as 3-D.
Applies to: Last Supper (Leonardo)

Definition: Painting on dry plaster; paint sits on the surface and flakes over time.
Applies to: Last Supper

Definition: "Smoky": Leonardo's soft, hazy blending of tones with no hard outlines.
Applies to: Leonardo's technique; best known from the Mona Lisa, not a focus work
